William Joyce (24 April 1906 – 3 January 1946), nicknamed Lord Haw-Haw, was an American-born British Fascist politician and Nazi propaganda broadcaster to the United Kingdom during World War II. He was convicted of one count of high treason in 1945, and sentenced to death. He was hanged at Wandsworth Prison on 3 January 1946, making him the last person to be executed for treason in the United Kingdom.

In 1932, Joyce joined the British Union of Fascists and swiftly became a leading speaker and in 1934 was promoted to the BUF's Director of Propaganda and later appointed deputy leader. In late August 1939, shortly before war was declared, Joyce and his wife Margaret fled to Germany where he was recruited for radio announcements and script writing at German radio's English service and became the best-known propaganda broadcaster. Initially an anonymous broadcaster, Joyce eventually revealed his real name to his listeners.

Although listening to his broadcasts was officially discouraged (but not illegal), many Britons did tune in. At the height of his influence, in 1940, Joyce had an estimated six million regular and 18 million occasional listeners in the United Kingdom. His broadcasts urged the British people to surrender and were well known for their jeering, sarcastic and menacing tone. There was also a desire by civilian listeners to hear what the other side was saying, since information during wartime was strictly censored.

On 28 May 1945 Joyce was captured by British forces at Flensburg, near the German border with Denmark. Shipped back to the UK, he was tried and convicted of treason and sentenced to be hanged. He went to his death unrepentant and defiant.
